instructions: Dice the onion, chop the tomatoes, mince the garlic and finely chop 1 1/2 tsp of ginger.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds. After about 20 seconds they will sizzle and smell toasty.
Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until soft and light golden.
Add the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes, until they are soft and mushy. Stir in the turmeric, chili powder and garam masala and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the frozen vegetables and cook for 1 minute. Pour in 5 cups water and the salt and bring it to a rolling boil. Reduce to medium and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the oats. Cook uncovered, stirring often, for about 5 minutes, until the oats are soft and the mixture is thick but still pourable. If it gets too thick, stir in hot water 1/4 cup at a time.
Take the pot off the heat. Stir in the juice of the lemon and 1/4 cup chopped cilantro. Taste it, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Slice the green chili and put it in a small bowl for the table. Serve the oats hot with the green chili on the side.
method_notes: Swasthi's Recipes (the lead) sautes cumin, onion, ginger, garlic and tomato with turmeric, chili and garam masala, adds vegetables and water, then stirs in rolled oats at the end and finishes with lemon and coriander. Piping Pot Curry agrees on the base but cooks steel-cut oats and uses less water. This is doubled for four, with frozen mixed vegetables to save chopping and the green chili moved to the table. It takes about 30 minutes in all, not 15.
